entries.title: abide
entries.summary: Remain, stay, dwell, continue — especially in Christ.
entries.fullSummary: "Abide in me, and I in you" is Jesus' invitation to stay close to Him moment by moment. In seasons when life feels unstable or your heart wants to run, abiding is the quiet answer. Small step: when anxiety or hurry rises today, pause and simply say, "Lord, I choose to abide in You right now."
entries.smallStep: In John 15, abide is staying joined to Christ, not visiting Him now and then.

entries.title: adoption
entries.summary: Placed as sons — privilege and Spirit witness.
entries.fullSummary: Adoption is more than a warm metaphor. It names a real change of status: no longer outside, no longer on probation, but welcomed as heirs in Christ.
entries.smallStep: Cry “Abba, Father” is Spirit-given confidence.

entries.title: alms
entries.summary: Merciful giving to the poor — not a performance.
entries.smallStep: Pair secret giving (Matthew 6) with a generous heart.

entries.title: amen
entries.summary: “So be it” — firm agreement and truth.
entries.smallStep: When Scripture stacks “amen,” treat it as sealed.

entries.title: anon
entries.summary: At once, soon — immediacy.
entries.smallStep: Rhymes with “upon” in rhythm — sense is “right away.”

entries.title: apostle
entries.summary: Sent one — eyewitness ambassadors of Christ with authority.
entries.smallStep: Distinguish the Twelve/foundation from every “sent” task today.

entries.title: array
entries.summary: Dress, equip, or set in order — not only “arrange data.”
entries.smallStep: In poetry, array is clothing and dignity.

entries.title: atonement
entries.summary: Covering of sin; fulfilled in the one final sacrifice.
entries.fullSummary: The old covenant sacrifices prepared the mind to understand Christ. Hebrews makes clear that all those coverings point forward to the one final offering that truly cleanses.
entries.smallStep: Hebrews shows one offering versus repeated shadows.

entries.title: authority
entries.summary: Power, right to command, or sphere — rulers, parents, Christ.
entries.smallStep: All human authority is under God’s.

entries.title: baptism
entries.summary: Immersion picture — union with Christ’s death and resurrection.
entries.fullSummary: Handle the word with both reverence and care. Scripture uses baptism as a sign tied closely to Christ and discipleship, while still distinguishing the sign from the Savior.
entries.smallStep: Distinguish sign from saving work — faith in Christ saves.

entries.title: begat
entries.summary: Fathered, brought forth — genealogy and incarnation language.
entries.smallStep: In Matthew 1, trace promise and fulfillment.

entries.title: begotten
entries.summary: Uniquely brought forth — “only begotten” points to the Son.
entries.smallStep: Hold uniqueness without drifting into confusion about the eternal Son.

entries.title: beguiled
entries.summary: Deceived, led astray — Eve and false teachers.
entries.smallStep: Name the lie; return to plain Scripture.

entries.title: beseech
entries.summary: Plead urgently, beg, or implore with deep feeling.
entries.smallStep: Hear beseech as gospel pleading, not casual suggestion.

entries.title: bewitched
entries.summary: Deceived or fascinated — not stage magic.
entries.smallStep: Paul’s point is gospel clarity stolen by confusion.

entries.title: bewray
entries.summary: Expose, reveal, betray — older verb.
entries.smallStep: Context shows whether betrayal or simple disclosure.

entries.title: bill
entries.summary: Written certificate — often divorce writing in controversy texts.
entries.smallStep: Jesus raises the heart, not paperwork tricks.

entries.title: bishop
entries.summary: Overseer — pastoral office of care and sound teaching.
entries.smallStep: Often overlaps elder; watch context for office vs gift.

entries.title: blasphemy
entries.summary: Speech that dishonors God or claims what is His alone.
entries.smallStep: Distinguish rash words from the unforgivable hardness Jesus warns of.

entries.title: blemish
entries.summary: Spot or defect — purity for sacrifice and character.
entries.smallStep: Christ is the spotless Lamb.

entries.title: blood
entries.summary: Life, sacrifice, covenant — context shows meaning.
entries.fullSummary: The Bible treats blood as weighty because life belongs to God. In Christ, blood language becomes the strong medicine of forgiveness, covenant, and cleansing.
entries.smallStep: Trace blood from altar to Christ once for all.

entries.title: blot out
entries.summary: Erase debt, remove from record — God’s forgiveness language.
entries.smallStep: Contrast with names kept in the book of life.

entries.title: bowels
entries.summary: Deep affection or compassion — idiom for the seat of feeling.
entries.fullSummary: "Bowels of mercies" or "bowels of compassion" point to gut-level mercy, the deep, moving compassion God has toward us and that we are to have toward others. This is not shallow sentiment. It is the same compassion that moved Jesus when He saw the multitudes. In parenting, marriage, or hard relationships, ask the Lord to fill your bowels with His mercy when you feel empty. It changes how you respond in the heat of the moment.
entries.smallStep: Read as “tender compassion,” not anatomy lessons.

entries.title: brasen
entries.summary: Brass or bronze — altar, serpent, sea (symbolic hardware).
entries.smallStep: Read as appointed instruments, not lucky charms.

entries.title: brazen
entries.summary: Often brass/bronze — brazen altar, brazen serpent.
entries.smallStep: The lifted serpent points to Christ — faith, not superstition.

entries.title: breath
entries.summary: Life-breath from God; also Spirit imagery.
entries.smallStep: Every breath is borrowed — live gratefully.

entries.title: bridegroom
entries.summary: Husband-to-be — Christ and the church imagery.
entries.smallStep: Joy and fidelity — not sentimental fluff.

entries.title: bruise
entries.summary: Crush or wound — Genesis 3:15 and the suffering Servant.
entries.smallStep: Trace hope from the first promise to the cross.

entries.title: buckler
entries.summary: Small shield — God as protector.
entries.smallStep: Pair with “shield” language in the same psalms.

entries.title: burden
entries.summary: Load, oracle, or heavy message — context picks.
entries.smallStep: “Burden” can mean prophetic word, not only weight.

entries.title: burthen
entries.summary: Older spelling of burden — same range of meaning.
entries.smallStep: Read smoothly as “burden.”

entries.title: bushel
entries.summary: Measure — hide or reveal light imagery.
entries.smallStep: Let good works shine for God’s glory, not vanity.

entries.title: by and by
entries.summary: Immediately or soon — not “eventually” in several texts.
entries.smallStep: Check context: sometimes “at once,” sometimes “later” in older English — compare translations carefully.

entries.title: candlestick
entries.summary: Lampstand — tabernacle and “light of the world” imagery.
entries.smallStep: Churches as lampstands is responsibility, not décor.

entries.title: carcase
entries.summary: Dead body — ceremonial laws and sober pictures.
entries.smallStep: Use reverence when reading death texts.

entries.title: careful
entries.summary: Often “full of care” or anxious, not merely “attentive.”
entries.fullSummary: This matters because "Be careful for nothing" is not telling you to be sloppy. It is telling anxious hearts to trade worry for prayer, thanksgiving, and trust.
entries.smallStep: Philippians 4:6 pairs “careful for nothing” with prayer.

entries.title: carefulness
entries.summary: Earnest care, godly zeal — can be grief-born attention.
entries.fullSummary: This is one of the places where scripture separates holy care from anxious spinning. In 2 Corinthians 7, carefulness is the awake, honest, responsible fruit of repentance, not fretfulness without movement.
entries.smallStep: 2 Corinthians 7:11 lists fruits of godly sorrow—carefulness is alert love.

entries.title: carnal
entries.summary: Fleshly, unspiritual — oriented by fallen appetite.
entries.smallStep: Not “body is bad,” but “self-run life” vs Spirit-led.

entries.title: carriage
entries.summary: Behavior or baggage — context decides (conduct vs what is carried).
entries.smallStep: In narrative, “carriage” can mean baggage train; in epistles, sometimes “walk.”

entries.title: cast
entries.summary: Throw upon, lay down, or hurl away — cares, nets, or garments by context.
entries.fullSummary: In care passages, cast is not vague coping language. It is a deliberate transfer of burden to God because He truly cares. Scripture treats this as an act of trust, not denial.
entries.smallStep: In care passages, cast is active release, not quiet denial.

entries.title: cast lots
entries.summary: Providence over chance — used for decisions in narrative.
entries.smallStep: God rules what looks random.

entries.title: chambering
entries.summary: Immoral bed-life — secret indulgence contrasted with daytime honor.
entries.fullSummary: The Bible uses this term to strip glamour from hidden sin. Chambering is secrecy without purity. The gospel answers it not with despair, but with daylight, repentance, and holiness that reaches private hours too.
entries.smallStep: Romans 13:13 pairs chambering with public decency—whole-life integrity.

entries.title: charity
entries.summary: Often means self-giving love (caritas), not fundraising or a donation drive.
entries.fullSummary: Paul uses it powerfully in 1 Corinthians 13: "Though I bestow all my goods to feed the poor, and though I give my body to be burned, and have not charity, it profiteth me nothing." This is love that puts others first even when no one is watching. In your daily battles, with family irritations, a hard neighbor, or your own exhaustion, this is the love that covers, bears, believes, hopes, and endures. It is Christ's love working in you. One small step: when tension rises today, quietly ask the Lord for His charity in that moment.
entries.smallStep: In 1 Corinthians 13, read “charity” as steadfast love.

entries.title: chaste
entries.summary: Pure in body and mind — modest love.
entries.smallStep: Chastity is wholeness, not shame of being human.

entries.title: chasten
entries.summary: Discipline for good — Fatherly correction.
entries.fullSummary: "Whom the Lord loveth he chasteneth." Chastening is the loving hand of a Father who wants us to share His holiness. In hard seasons that feel like punishment, this word brings comfort: the Lord is not against you; He is training you. Small step: when correction or hardship comes today, receive it as the Lord's loving chastening and ask Him to produce the peaceable fruit of righteousness.
entries.smallStep: Receive discipline as love, not rejection.

entries.title: chastise
entries.summary: Correct sharply when needed — still purposeful.
entries.smallStep: Distinguish human abuse from God’s righteous rule.

entries.title: cherubims
entries.summary: Cherubim — heavenly guardians and throne imagery.
entries.smallStep: Holy presence is not casual.

entries.title: church
entries.summary: Assembly — local gathered body and Christ’s people overall.
entries.fullSummary: This word protects against reducing church to a building or brand. The church is Christ's gathered people, loved by Him and formed under His word.
entries.smallStep: Building metaphor is people, not brick idolatry.

entries.title: circumspect
entries.summary: Careful, watchful, prudent in conduct.
entries.smallStep: Walk circumspectly means step with wisdom, not panic.

entries.title: cleave
entries.summary: Cling to, stick fast, or adhere closely — by context it can also mean split apart.
entries.fullSummary: "Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother, and shall cleave unto his wife." This word pictures a strong, lasting bond. In your battles with distraction, loneliness, or wavering faith, the Lord invites you to cleave to Him with all your heart. Small step: when you feel pulled in many directions today, intentionally cleave to one promise from Scripture and hold fast.
entries.smallStep: Marriage cleaving and covenant loyalty both mean hold fast — watch the verse.

entries.title: cloak
entries.summary: Outer garment — justice, travel, and generosity scenes.
entries.fullSummary: Cloak is not a random wardrobe detail in scripture. In law and teaching it becomes a test of how you treat vulnerability, rights, and neighbor-love. Jesus uses it to stretch the heart beyond strict self-protection.
entries.smallStep: Matthew 5:40 is radical generosity—read as Jesus’ kingdom ethic, not coercion.

entries.title: closet
entries.summary: Private inner room for prayer, not a clothes closet only.
entries.fullSummary: Jesus is describing private prayer away from display. The force of the word is secrecy and nearness with the Father, not impressive setup.
entries.smallStep: Picture a shut door and secret speech to the Father.

entries.title: clothed
entries.summary: Put on — often moral or gospel clothing imagery.
entries.smallStep: “Put on Christ” is daily dressing by faith.

entries.title: comely
entries.summary: Beautiful, fitting, or becoming — not just pretty.
entries.fullSummary: "I am black, but comely" and "Praise is comely for the upright." This word speaks of beauty that is proper and honoring to God. In a world obsessed with outward looks, comely reminds us that quiet dignity and godly conduct are truly beautiful. Small step: choose one modest, fitting action today that honors the Lord.
entries.smallStep: Comely beauty is fitting and honorable — dignity without show.

entries.title: comfortable
entries.summary: Comforting words or strength — adjective of comfort.
entries.smallStep: “Comfort ye” goes with tender speech.

entries.title: commend
entries.summary: Entrust, commit, praise — several shades.
entries.smallStep: Paul commends people to God’s grace — a tender charge.

entries.title: communed
entries.summary: Spoke closely, counseled — intimate talk.
entries.smallStep: “Commune with your own heart” is honest self-talk before God.

entries.title: communicate
entries.summary: Often “share” or give materially, not only “talk.”
entries.fullSummary: This word often moves from speech to generosity. The Bible is teaching shared life, where truth and tangible care belong together.
entries.smallStep: Hebrews 13:16 ties sharing with doing good.

entries.title: communion
entries.summary: Fellowship — often Lord’s supper sense in older usage.
entries.fullSummary: The word presses against isolated faith. Communion is shared participation in Christ and a reminder that private belief grows inside a living body.
entries.smallStep: 1 Corinthians 10 ties cup and bread to one body.

entries.title: compass
entries.summary: Surround, encircle, go round — siege and prayer language.
entries.fullSummary: When trouble compasses you, scripture is naming a real feeling of being hemmed in. That honesty makes the Psalms good companions in fear: they tell the truth about pressure while still leaning on the Lord inside the circle.
entries.smallStep: If trouble “compasses” you, picture being hemmed in—then remember who is nearer still.

entries.title: comprehend
entries.summary: Sometimes “overcome” or “take hold of,” not only “understand.”
entries.smallStep: John 1:5: darkness did not overcome the light.

entries.title: concision
entries.summary: Mutilation — Paul’s sharp word for fleshly confidence.
entries.smallStep: Contrast true circumcision of heart by the Spirit.

entries.title: concupiscence
entries.summary: Strong desire, lust — inner pull toward wrong delight.
entries.fullSummary: Concupiscence is helpful because it names sin before it becomes an outward act. Scripture traces the problem back to inward appetite, where prayer, truth, and mortification have to begin.
entries.smallStep: Trace James 1:14–15 from desire to death—early kill the bud with truth and prayer.

entries.title: condemnation
entries.summary: Judgment — guilty verdict; contrast “no condemnation” in Christ.
entries.fullSummary: The force of Romans 8:1 shines only when condemnation is heard clearly. Christ does not merely soothe guilty feelings; He removes the verdict for those in Him.
entries.smallStep: Romans 8:1 is the anchor verse for assurance.

entries.title: confound
entries.summary: Confuse, shame, bring to nothing.
entries.smallStep: God frustrates proud schemes.

entries.title: conscience
entries.summary: Inner witness — trained by truth, not mere feelings.
entries.smallStep: A seared conscience is dangerous — feed it Scripture.

entries.title: constrained
entries.summary: Pressed, compelled, or strongly moved — not cold force.
entries.fullSummary: "The love of Christ constraineth us." This is not cold duty but a holy pressure that moves us forward. Christ's love becomes the gentle force that keeps us going when we want to quit. Small step: when you feel weary or tempted to pull back today, remember the love of Christ that constrains you and let it carry you one more step.
entries.smallStep: Let Christ’s love move you more than fear does.

entries.title: convenient
entries.summary: Suitable timing or opportunity — not merely “handy.”
entries.fullSummary: This word often reveals the moral use of timing. Sometimes convenience serves wisdom; sometimes it becomes a shield for delay, indulgence, or cowardice. Felix is the warning case: a more convenient season never becomes repentance.
entries.smallStep: Herod’s “convenient day” is planned indulgence—watch when convenience serves sin.

entries.title: conversation
entries.summary: Usually manner of life or citizenship, not small talk.
entries.fullSummary: It is your whole pattern of life, what people see when they watch how you handle pressure, family, money, and speech. This word calls us to live as citizens of heaven right in the middle of earthly battles. In 2026 hurry and noise, a godly conversation becomes a quiet testimony. Small step: choose one ordinary moment today, a conversation with your child or a reply at work, and let it reflect the gospel.
entries.smallStep: Ask: “How is my walk?” when you see “conversation.”

entries.title: convert
entries.summary: Turn back, restore — soul and direction.
entries.smallStep: Conversion is Godward turn, not a mood.

entries.title: corn
entries.summary: Grain (wheat, barley), not maize.
entries.fullSummary: Reading this as grain keeps harvest passages clear and grounded in Bible-land agriculture. It preserves the ordinary field imagery the passage expects you to picture.
entries.smallStep: Picture sheaves and harvest, not sweet corn on the cob.

entries.title: couch
entries.summary: Lie down, rest — sheep and sleep imagery.
entries.smallStep: Picture calm when the Lord makes His people lie down.

entries.title: covenant
entries.summary: Binding promise God makes and keeps; new covenant in Christ’s blood.
entries.fullSummary: The Bible does not present salvation as vague good intentions. Covenant language shows God binding Himself by promise, climaxing in the new covenant sealed by Christ's blood.
entries.smallStep: Old and new contrast in Hebrews is about better promises.

entries.title: creeping
entries.summary: Crawling things — creation categories and purity laws.
entries.smallStep: Order in creation; humility before the Creator.

entries.title: cross
entries.summary: Shameful death and glory — offense and power.
entries.fullSummary: Never let the familiarity of the word soften its scandal. The cross is where judgment, mercy, victory, and self-denial all meet in Christ.
entries.smallStep: Boast only in the Lord’s finished work.

entries.title: crucify
entries.summary: Nail to a cross — old man, flesh, and Christ’s death.
entries.smallStep: Union with Christ’s death is real, not metaphor only.

entries.title: cruel
entries.summary: Harsh, fierce — character and consequences.
entries.smallStep: Cruel masters contrast the gentle yoke of Christ.

entries.title: cup
entries.summary: Cup of blessing or wrath — what you drink with God.
entries.smallStep: Jesus drank the bitter cup for us.

entries.title: curious
entries.summary: Skilled, intricate, or prying — context picks.
entries.smallStep: Craftsmanship vs forbidden arts — watch the verse.

entries.title: curseth
entries.summary: Calls down curse — solemn, not slang.
entries.smallStep: Bless those who curse you — Romans 12.

entries.title: custom
entries.summary: Habit, tax, or ordinary practice — context decides.
entries.smallStep: “After the custom” is routine — not necessarily holy.

entries.title: cut off
entries.summary: Removed from covenant people or life — serious.
entries.smallStep: Let the weight point you to Christ’s sufficient sacrifice.

entries.title: damnation
entries.summary: Condemnation or judgment — legal outcome, not a curse word.
entries.smallStep: Serious, not slang — let the text define which judgment.

entries.title: defiled
entries.summary: Made unclean — ceremonial or moral.
entries.smallStep: Wash in confession and truth — 1 John 1:9.

entries.title: deliver
entries.summary: Rescue, hand over, or birth — track the sense.
entries.smallStep: Deliver us from evil is daily dependence.

entries.title: deliverance
entries.summary: Rescue realized — God’s help in trouble.
entries.smallStep: Remember past deliverances when new fears rise.

entries.title: deny
entries.summary: Disown, refuse — Jesus warns and encourages.
entries.smallStep: Self-denial follows Christ — not self-hatred.

entries.title: depart
entries.summary: Go away, remove, or die — gentle or solemn.
entries.smallStep: “Depart from me” is sober when Jesus says it.

entries.title: despise
entries.summary: Treat as nothing — God, wisdom, or neighbor.
entries.smallStep: Do not despise small beginnings of grace.

entries.title: devils
entries.summary: Demons, unclean spirits — Christ’s authority is absolute.
entries.smallStep: No fascination — flee to Christ’s word and presence.

entries.title: devour
entries.summary: Consume — Satan as roaring lion; strife devours.
entries.smallStep: Stay sober; resist him steadfast in faith.

entries.title: diligence
entries.summary: Steady effort — faith and virtue.
entries.smallStep: Diligence is quiet faithfulness, not panic.

entries.title: diligent
entries.summary: Careful, persistent effort — earnest and thorough work.
entries.smallStep: Diligence is steady care, not frantic strain.

entries.title: discreet
entries.summary: Sensible, prudent — especially Titus 2 maturity.
entries.smallStep: Discretion defuses many fires.

entries.title: discretion
entries.summary: Good judgment, prudence — moral taste and timing.
entries.fullSummary: The Bible treats discretion as a guardian, not a personality quirk. It helps love arrive at the right time, in the right measure, without becoming cowardly or harsh.
entries.smallStep: Proverbs ties discretion to keeping paths—wisdom guards love.

entries.title: dissimulation
entries.summary: Hypocrisy — hiding what you truly are.
entries.smallStep: Love without dissimulation is sincere brotherly love.

entries.title: divers
entries.summary: Various — older spelling of diverse.
entries.smallStep: Read “divers” as “many kinds,” not scuba.

entries.title: doctrine
entries.summary: Teaching — sound words to build and guard.
entries.smallStep: Test all teaching by Christ and the apostles.

entries.title: draught
entries.summary: Catch of fish; also drain — context picks.
entries.smallStep: Miraculous draughts show who rules sea and heart.

entries.title: dross
entries.summary: Waste slag from metal — impurity to purge.
entries.smallStep: Refining imagery: God purges, not to destroy you.

entries.title: drunken
entries.summary: Intoxicated — warning and watchfulness.
entries.smallStep: Be filled with the Spirit instead — Ephesians 5.

entries.title: dumb
entries.summary: Mute, speechless — not modern insult.
entries.smallStep: Healing stories restore voice — picture gospel opening mouths.

entries.title: durst
entries.summary: Dared — older past of dare.
entries.smallStep: Swap “dared” mentally when you hit durst.

entries.title: earnest
entries.summary: A pledge, guarantee, or first installment.
entries.fullSummary: The Holy Spirit is given as the earnest of our inheritance. He is God's guarantee that everything He has promised will one day be fully ours. In days when the battle feels long, this word is quiet assurance: the Spirit inside you is the first payment on glory. Small step: thank the Lord today for the earnest of the Spirit already living in you.
entries.smallStep: The Spirit is God’s earnest that glory is truly coming.

entries.title: edify
entries.summary: Build up or strengthen spiritually — like raising a house.
entries.fullSummary: "Let all things be done unto edifying." Our words, actions, and time together should build one another up in Christ. In family tension or church struggles, choose what edifies rather than tears down. Small step: speak or do one thing today that strengthens someone else's faith.
entries.smallStep: Ask: does this word build or tear down?

entries.title: elder
entries.summary: Older man; also office of oversight — context.
entries.smallStep: Respect and honor where Scripture commands.

entries.title: election
entries.summary: God’s choosing — comfort and humility, not arrogance.
entries.smallStep: Hold election with calling and holiness.

entries.title: embrace
entries.summary: Hold fast — wisdom, seasons, people.
entries.smallStep: Ecclesiastes pairs embrace with refraining — seasons.

entries.title: emulation
entries.summary: Jealous rivalry, zealous contention — not modern “emulate a hero.”
entries.fullSummary: The word belongs in the works-of-the-flesh list because rivalry can wear a respectable face. Emulation turns another person's gift into a threat and quietly trains the heart to compete instead of love.
entries.smallStep: Works of the flesh include emulations—compare yourself less; bless more.

entries.title: end
entries.summary: Goal, outcome, or final stop — teleology matters.
entries.smallStep: “The end of your faith” is salvation of souls.

entries.title: engender
entries.summary: Begets, produces — James on lust.
entries.smallStep: Trace sin’s birth to death; grace’s birth to life.

entries.title: ensample
entries.summary: Pattern or example left for others to follow.
entries.fullSummary: We are called to be ensamples, patterns, to the flock. Your quiet faithfulness in hard days can become someone else's roadmap. Small step: live one ordinary moment today as a gentle pattern of trust for those watching.
entries.smallStep: Christ’s steps are the template in 1 Peter 2:21.

entries.title: ensue
entries.summary: Follow after, pursue, or chase — often peace.
entries.smallStep: Do not wait for peace to happen — pursue it on purpose.

entries.title: envious
entries.summary: Jealous of another’s good — rots bones.
entries.smallStep: Rejoice with those who rejoice — kill envy.

entries.title: epistle
entries.summary: Letter — apostolic mail to churches.
entries.smallStep: These letters are God-breathed rule for faith.

entries.title: err
entries.summary: Wander off course — morally and intellectually.
entries.smallStep: Gentle restoration for the erring — James 5.

entries.title: eschew
entries.summary: Turn aside from; shun evil.
entries.smallStep: Pair with “seek peace” in the same verse.

entries.title: espoused
entries.summary: Betrothed — purity and expectation.
entries.smallStep: Paul’s bridal language is devotion, not drama.

entries.title: esteem
entries.summary: Value, regard, or reckon — context picks.
entries.smallStep: Esteem others better — humility in community.

entries.title: everlasting
entries.summary: Age-enduring, eternal — God’s life and punishment both serious.
entries.smallStep: Let context show gift of life or severity of judgment.

entries.title: exhort
entries.summary: Strongly encourage — apostolic voice.
entries.smallStep: Exhortation is love with backbone.

entries.title: eyeservice
entries.summary: Service only when watched — hollow obedience.
entries.smallStep: Serve as unto the Lord — heart, not performance.

entries.title: fain
entries.summary: Gladly, willingly, or with desire.
entries.fullSummary: The prodigal would fain have filled his belly with the husks. This word reveals deep longing. In our own battles with lesser things, fain reminds us we were made for more. Small step: when you catch yourself reaching for something empty today, turn that fain desire toward the Father who runs to meet you.
entries.smallStep: Let deep desire turn you toward the Father, not husks.

entries.title: faint
entries.summary: Grow weak, lose heart — God strengthens.
entries.fullSummary: "They that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles; they shall run, and not be weary; and they shall walk, and not faint." This is for the exhausted parent, the discouraged believer, the tired laborer. Small step: when you feel faint today, pause and wait on the Lord, even for one quiet minute.
entries.smallStep: Do not faint in well doing — season of reaping comes.

entries.title: faith
entries.summary: Trust resting on God’s word; shows in obedience.
entries.fullSummary: Faith receives what grace gives. It does not compete with obedience; living faith leans on God so deeply that obedience begins to grow from the inside out.
entries.smallStep: Faith and works tensions resolve when faith is living.

entries.title: familiar spirit
entries.summary: Forbidden spirit contact — witchcraft territory.
entries.smallStep: Seek the Lord, not the dead — sober warning.

entries.title: fast
entries.summary: Abstain food for prayer — not “quick.”
entries.smallStep: Fasting pairs with feasting on God’s word.

entries.title: fat
entries.summary: Rich, best portion — offerings and abundance.
entries.smallStep: “Fatness” can mean deep satisfaction in God.

entries.title: fatlings
entries.summary: Young fat cattle — feast and sacrifice imagery.
entries.smallStep: Parables use feast language — come to the banquet.

entries.title: fear
entries.summary: Reverence or terror — context shows holy fear vs panic.
entries.fullSummary: Scripture does not flatten all fear into one category. It removes slavish terror while teaching reverent trembling before the Lord who is holy and good.
entries.smallStep: “Fear not” calms panic; “fear God” awakens reverence.

entries.title: fearfully
entries.summary: Wonderfully — awe, not terror, in Psalm 139.
entries.smallStep: You are fearfully set apart — dignity from the Maker.

entries.title: fetch
entries.summary: Go get, bring — plain narrative verb.
entries.smallStep: Swap “go get” mentally when fetch appears—story keeps moving.

entries.title: fiends
entries.summary: Fierce companions or mockers — rare word.
entries.smallStep: Job’s loneliness language — read with compassion.

entries.title: filthy
entries.summary: Morally foul — rags, speech, lucre.
entries.smallStep: Christ clothes the filthy with righteousness.

entries.title: firmament
entries.summary: Expanse or arch — heavens spread out, not modern “firm plate” debates.
entries.smallStep: Read poetry as majesty, not modern science footnotes in the margin.

entries.title: firstborn
entries.summary: Preeminent heir — Israel, Christ, church.
entries.smallStep: Christ is firstborn among many brethren.

entries.title: firstfruits
entries.summary: First part of harvest — pledge of full crop.
entries.smallStep: Resurrection is firstfruits — more glory coming.

entries.title: flattery
entries.summary: Smooth words that mislead — guard the naive.
entries.smallStep: Love speaks truth with kindness.

entries.title: flesh
entries.summary: Body, human nature, kinship, or weakness — context decides.
entries.fullSummary: This is one of the most important context words in the KJV. Sometimes it is simple embodiment; sometimes it is self-directed life resisting the Spirit.
entries.smallStep: Track whether “flesh” means body, self, or unredeemed appetite.

entries.title: fleshly
entries.summary: According to the flesh — unspiritual mindset.
entries.smallStep: Not “body bad,” but “self on the throne.”

entries.title: forbear
entries.summary: Refrain, hold back, or be patient with.
entries.smallStep: Forbearance chooses not to strike back in haste.

entries.title: fowls
entries.summary: Birds — care of God and parable seed.
entries.smallStep: If God feeds fowls, He will sustain you.

entries.title: frankincense
entries.summary: Incense offering — prayer and worship aroma.
entries.smallStep: Picture tabernacle worship — Christ is better.

entries.title: freewill
entries.summary: Voluntary offering — glad heart.
entries.smallStep: God loves a cheerful giver — 2 Corinthians 9.

entries.title: froward
entries.summary: Stubbornly contrary, perverse, or difficult to deal with.
entries.fullSummary: The Lord is good even to the froward. This word names the crooked, contrary part of the human heart. Yet God still shows kindness to the froward. Small step: when you feel your own froward spirit rising today, ask the Lord to make you gentle where you are naturally contrary.
entries.smallStep: Ask God to soften what is crooked or contrary in you.

entries.title: gainsay
entries.summary: Speak against, contradict — opposition.
entries.fullSummary: "That he may be able... to convince the gainsayers." Gainsayers are those who speak against the truth. The Lord gives us both courage and wisdom not to be silenced. Small step: when someone contradicts truth in your hearing today, respond with gentle confidence instead of fear.
entries.smallStep: Christ’s witnesses speak boldly when opposed.

entries.title: gender
entries.summary: Beget, produce — archaic verb “gendereth.”
entries.smallStep: James: lust conceives and sins when full grown.

entries.title: gentiles
entries.summary: Nations — non-Jewish peoples; grace to the world.
entries.smallStep: One new man — Jew and Gentile in Christ.

entries.title: ghost
entries.summary: Holy Ghost is the Holy Spirit — older English for the same Person.
entries.fullSummary: Do not import modern spooky associations into this word. The KJV is speaking of the same Holy Spirit promised by Christ, present to comfort, teach, and empower.
entries.smallStep: Do not read “ghost” as a spooky figure; same Comforter Jesus promised.

entries.title: gird
entries.summary: Prepare, brace, or arm yourself for action — like tightening a belt.
entries.fullSummary: "Wherefore gird up the loins of your mind." This is a call to mental and spiritual readiness for the day's battles. Small step: before you step into your responsibilities today, quietly gird your mind with truth, one verse, one prayer, one steadying thought.
entries.smallStep: “Gird up the loins of your mind” is alert holiness.

entries.title: girdle
entries.summary: Belt — priestly dress and John the Baptist.
entries.smallStep: Symbol of strength and office — read visually.

entries.title: glean
entries.summary: Gather leftovers — mercy for the poor.
entries.smallStep: Boaz’s field is a picture of generous provision.

entries.title: glede
entries.summary: Bird of prey — eagle-like in prophecy.
entries.smallStep: Rare word — read as swift destroying bird in judgment poetry.

entries.title: gospel
entries.summary: Good news of Christ’s kingdom, death, and resurrection.
entries.fullSummary: The gospel is not a vague religious mood. It is public good news about what God has done in Christ, and it comes with saving power for those who believe.
entries.smallStep: Keep the core facts central when “gospel” is used broadly.

entries.title: grace
entries.summary: God’s favor you did not earn — not permission to sin.
entries.fullSummary: Grace is more than a doorway word. It is the atmosphere of Christian life from start to finish: pardon for the guilty and strength for the weak.
entries.smallStep: Pair Ephesians 2:8–9 with Romans 6 on new life.

entries.title: hale
entries.summary: Drag or pull roughly — often by force.
entries.fullSummary: "Lest he hale thee to the judge." This word pictures forceful dragging. In spiritual battles we can feel haled by fear, guilt, or pressure. Christ never hales us; He gently leads. Small step: when you feel dragged by anxiety or accusation today, come to the Lord who draws instead of drags.
entries.smallStep: Christ leads gently; fear and accusation try to drag.

entries.title: halting
entries.summary: Limping, wavering between two ways — physical or spiritual.
entries.fullSummary: Halting in Elijah's challenge is more than indecision. It is divided allegiance. Scripture uses the image well because spiritual wobbling feels like limping: unstable, tiring, and hard to hide for long.
entries.smallStep: Elijah’s “halt ye between two opinions” is decide whom you will serve.

entries.title: haply
entries.summary: Perhaps, maybe — not “happily.”
entries.smallStep: Think “perhaps,” not emotional happiness.

entries.title: harlot
entries.summary: Prostitute — literal and covenant unfaithfulness imagery.
entries.smallStep: Spiritual adultery is chasing lovers that cannot save.

entries.title: haste
entries.summary: Hurry — sometimes wise, sometimes rash.
entries.smallStep: Wait on the Lord beats proud haste.

entries.title: haughty
entries.summary: Lifted up in pride — God resists.
entries.fullSummary: Haughtiness matters because scripture treats it as more than bad manners. It is an inward rising above creaturely place. The Bible answers it with humility before God, not with self-hatred but with right-sizedness.
entries.smallStep: Humble yourself under God’s hand — 1 Peter 5:6.

entries.title: hearken
entries.summary: Listen and obey — covenant call.
entries.fullSummary: This word keeps scripture from becoming mere information. To hearken is to bend the ear and the life together. That is why prophets and psalms use it in covenant language so often.
entries.smallStep: Hearkening is more than ears — it is doing.

entries.title: heart
entries.summary: Will, mind, and inner person — not only emotion.
entries.fullSummary: Scripture treats the heart as the command center of a life. That is why guarding it matters: what rules the heart eventually shapes words, habits, and worship.
entries.smallStep: “As he thinketh in his heart” is orientation, not only mood.

entries.title: heaviness
entries.summary: Grief, depression of spirit — God meets it.
entries.fullSummary: Heaviness is not faithlessness by itself. Scripture gives language for burdened souls and then brings promise near them. God does not shame the heavy; He meets them with comfort, hope, and oil for mourning.
entries.smallStep: Oil of joy for heaviness — Isaiah 61.

entries.title: hell
entries.summary: Sheol, grave, or Gehenna by context — not one English place every time.
entries.smallStep: Let surrounding verses show whether grave, judgment, or imagery.

entries.title: hell fire
entries.summary: Gehenna imagery — Jesus warns seriously.
entries.smallStep: Read warnings with trembling mercy — flee to Christ.

entries.title: holiness
entries.summary: Set-apartness unto God — moral and positional.
entries.fullSummary: The word is not about sterile distance from ordinary life. It is life increasingly claimed by God, shaped by His beauty, and cleansed from double-mindedness.
entries.smallStep: Pursue peace and holiness together.

entries.title: holpen
entries.summary: Helped, assisted, or supported — older form of “helped.”
entries.smallStep: Hear holpen as remembered help from the Lord.

entries.title: hope
entries.summary: Confident expectation anchored in God, not wishfulness.
entries.fullSummary: Hope is a future-facing word, but it works in the present. It steadies grief, energizes patience, and keeps despair from getting the final sentence.
entries.smallStep: Hope is sure because the Promiser is faithful.

entries.title: husbandman
entries.summary: Farmer, tiller, or caretaker of a vineyard.
entries.fullSummary: "My Father is the husbandman." God is the careful farmer who prunes, waters, and waits for fruit. He knows exactly what each branch needs. Small step: in any area that feels barren or pruned today, remember you are under the hand of the perfect Husbandman.
entries.smallStep: Trust the patient hand of the Husbandman over your growth.

entries.title: imputation
entries.summary: Counted to your account — Abraham’s faith reckoned as righteousness (idea in Romans 4).
entries.smallStep: Follow “reckon” and “impute” in Romans 4 in one sitting.

entries.title: instant
entries.summary: Urgent, persistent, or at once — not only a moment in time.
entries.fullSummary: "Rejoicing in hope; patient in tribulation; continuing instant in prayer." This word calls us to pray without ceasing, steady, urgent, ongoing. In busy 2026 life, instant in prayer is a lifeline. Small step: turn one ordinary moment today into an instant prayer.
entries.smallStep: “Instant in prayer” means steady, ready prayer.

entries.title: intercession
entries.summary: Praying for another — Christ and the Spirit.
entries.fullSummary: This word matters on prayerless days. The Bible teaches not only that we should pray, but that the Son and the Spirit continue to help and carry prayer when we are weak.
entries.smallStep: Christ’s priesthood is ongoing help.

entries.title: intreat
entries.summary: Plead with, ask earnestly, or make a strong request.
entries.fullSummary: "Intreat the younger as brethren." This word carries respectful, heartfelt pleading. It is how we are to speak to one another and how we come to God. Small step: when you need to correct or encourage someone today, do it with the gentle tone of intreat.
entries.smallStep: Correct and encourage with the tone of intreat, not harshness.

entries.title: Isaiah 54:10
entries.summary: For the mountains shall depart, and the hills be removed; but my kindness shall not depart from thee, neither shall the covenant of my peace be removed, saith the LORD that hath mercy on thee.
entries.smallStep: Let today's verse stay close and carry only the next step.

entries.title: issue
entries.summary: Outflow, discharge, or result — what flows out matters.
entries.smallStep: Guard the issues of the heart so good things flow out.

entries.title: jot
entries.summary: The smallest letter — the tiniest detail.
entries.fullSummary: "Till heaven and earth pass, one jot or one tittle shall in no wise pass from the law." Jesus cares about the smallest strokes of Scripture. Nothing in God's Word is insignificant. Small step: when you read a tiny detail in your Bible today, thank the Lord that not even a jot will fail.
entries.smallStep: Thank God that not even the smallest stroke of His Word fails.

entries.title: joy
entries.summary: Deep gladness rooted in God — not hype.
entries.fullSummary: Joy can live beside tears because its root is deeper than mood. The Bible gives joy as fruit, gift, and strength in the presence of God.
entries.smallStep: Joy can coexist with grief when hope holds.

entries.title: justified
entries.summary: Declared righteous before God by faith — not “earned by behavior first.”
entries.fullSummary: You hear the gospel more clearly when this stays legal and relational. God justifies the ungodly by faith in Christ, then begins the lifelong work of renewal.
entries.smallStep: Distinguish standing before God from growth in holiness.

entries.title: leasing
entries.summary: Lying, falsehood — old noun for empty words.
entries.fullSummary: The word is useful because it keeps deceit from sounding sophisticated. Leasing is speech that wastes reality. In the Psalms it often stands near vanity, showing how falsehood empties both worship and neighbor-love.
entries.smallStep: Pair leasing with vanity in Psalm 4—speech that cannot hold weight.

entries.title: let
entries.summary: Often “allow” or “permit,” sometimes “leave off.”
entries.fullSummary: "Only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way." Here let means restrain or hold back. In daily battles, we sometimes need the Lord to let, hinder, wrong desires or to allow good things in His timing. Small step: when something feels blocked today, pause and ask whether the Lord is letting, restraining, for your protection.
entries.smallStep: When Paul says “I beseech you… let,” he means “allow this to be so.”

entries.title: list
entries.summary: To choose, desire, or please — archaic verb.
entries.smallStep: “Listed” can mean “was pleased” or “chose.”

entries.title: longsuffering
entries.summary: Patience, slow anger — fruit of the Spirit.
entries.fullSummary: The Lord is longsuffering toward us. He gives us time to repent, and He asks us to show the same to others, especially in family and parenting. Small step: when irritation rises today, ask for Christ's longsuffering to flow through you.
entries.smallStep: God’s longsuffering is room to repent.

entries.title: lowliness
entries.summary: Humility, lowliness of mind — freedom from pride.
entries.smallStep: Lowliness is quiet strength, not self-hatred.

entries.title: lucre
entries.summary: Gain, money — often “filthy lucre” when gain corrupts.
entries.fullSummary: The danger in lucre is not earning money honestly, but letting gain bend character and ministry. Scripture brings this word near shepherding and leadership because greed can quietly rot service from the inside.
entries.smallStep: Office lists warn against greedy patterns—love people more than leverage.

entries.title: lust
entries.summary: Strong desire — not only sexual; can be craving generally.
entries.fullSummary: The flesh lusts against the Spirit. But the psalmist also says, "My soul longeth, yea, even fainteth for the courts of the Lord." This word reminds us that desire itself is powerful and must be directed toward Christ. Small step: when a wrong craving rises, redirect it by speaking a verse of holy longing.
entries.smallStep: Name the desire and bring it to God honestly.

entries.title: magnify
entries.summary: Make great, exalt, or declare the greatness of.
entries.smallStep: Magnify the Lord by naming His greatness out loud.

entries.title: mammon
entries.summary: Riches as a rival master — loyalty, not mere money.
entries.fullSummary: Mammon matters because Jesus personalizes the danger. Money is not just a tool; it can become a lord. The heart question is not how much you possess, but where you look for safety, status, and control.
entries.smallStep: Matthew 6:24 is about single-hearted service—God or competing trust.

entries.title: matrix
entries.summary: Womb — where life begins under God’s numbering.
entries.fullSummary: This is a sacred-life word, not a strange technicality. The firstborn laws remind Israel that life, birth, and belonging are under God's claim. The strangeness of the term can hide the tenderness of the truth if read too quickly.
entries.smallStep: Firstborn and matrix texts show life belongs to God—read reverently.

entries.title: meat
entries.summary: Often solid food (teaching you chew on), not only animal flesh.
entries.fullSummary: Jesus said, "My meat is to do the will of him that sent me." This shows how real spiritual food satisfies the soul. In seasons when you feel spiritually empty or when parenting feels like constant feeding, remember: Christ Himself is the true meat that strengthens. Small step: when you feel weak or drained today, ask the Lord to feed you with His will and Word.
entries.smallStep: Contrast milk and meat when growth in doctrine is in view.

entries.title: meddle
entries.summary: Busy oneself in what is not yours — warn trouble.
entries.smallStep: Ask: “Is this my lane?”

entries.title: meek
entries.summary: Strength under God’s hand — not weakness.
entries.fullSummary: The meek are not people with no strength. They are people whose strength is submitted, teachable, and unwilling to seize by force what God will give in season.
entries.smallStep: Meekness trusts God with outcomes.

entries.title: meet
entries.summary: Fitting, suitable, right for the purpose — not always “encounter.”
entries.fullSummary: "It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him an help meet for him." Meet here means perfectly suited and corresponding. God still provides what is meet for His children. Small step: thank the Lord today for ways He has already given you what is meet for your situation.
entries.smallStep: In Genesis 2:18, “help meet” means suitable helper—dignity, not inferiority.

entries.title: mercy
entries.summary: Steadfast love and compassion — not getting what you deserve.
entries.fullSummary: Mercy is not less than forgiveness, but broader. It is God stooping toward need, not because the need is attractive, but because His heart is.
entries.smallStep: Mercy grounds hope on hard days.

entries.title: mortify
entries.summary: Put to death — kill sin by the Spirit’s help.
entries.fullSummary: Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth. This is not self-effort but Spirit-empowered dying to sin so we can live to Christ. Small step: name one sin pattern that needs mortifying and ask the Holy Spirit to help you put it to death today.
entries.smallStep: Not self-harm — Spirit-empowered putting off.

entries.title: multiply
entries.summary: Increase, grow many — people, blessing, or trouble by context.
entries.smallStep: Ask whether growth is godly or grievous.

entries.title: napkin
entries.summary: Cloth — face wrapping, burial detail, stewardship parable.
entries.fullSummary: Napkin passages are small-detail passages, but scripture often stores meaning there. In John 20 the ordered cloth quietly witnesses to a risen Lord who was not stolen in panic. In Luke 19 the wrapped coin exposes fearful stewardship.
entries.smallStep: John 20:7: folded napkin signals orderly resurrection hope.

entries.title: new birth
entries.summary: Born again — Spirit’s work, not mere decision talk.
entries.fullSummary: The gospel does not only repair the old life. New birth means God gives life where there was only fleshly inability, and He does it by His Spirit and word.
entries.smallStep: Nicodemus needed Spirit, not only argument.

entries.title: notwithstanding
entries.summary: Nevertheless, in spite of that, or although.
entries.fullSummary: "Notwithstanding the Lord stood with me." This word carries triumphant faith in the middle of hard facts. It says, "This is true... but God is greater." Small step: when circumstances are against you today, speak a quiet "notwithstanding the Lord is with me."
entries.smallStep: Let notwithstanding become a word of faith in hard facts.

entries.title: occupy
entries.summary: Use, employ, or be busy with faithfully — not just take up space.
entries.fullSummary: "Occupy till I come." Jesus calls us to be faithful with what He has given us until He returns. In daily work, parenting, or ministry, occupy means to use your time and gifts well. Small step: whatever is in your hands today, occupy it faithfully for the King.
entries.smallStep: Occupy what God placed in your hands until He comes.

entries.title: offence
entries.summary: Stumbling block — trap or cause to fall.
entries.fullSummary: This keeps the moral edge of the word intact. An offence in scripture may be something that trips a conscience, derails a disciple, or places a snare in the path.
entries.smallStep: Love limits liberty when others stumble.

entries.title: peace
entries.summary: Shalom — wholeness, rest, reconciliation; not only feelings.
entries.fullSummary: Some verses speak of peace with God; others of the peace of God. Both matter: one is reconciliation accomplished, the other is rest experienced in that reconciliation.
entries.smallStep: Distinguish Christ’s gift from the world’s distraction.

entries.title: peculiar
entries.summary: Treasured possession or special people set apart, not “weird.”
entries.fullSummary: "Peculiar people" means a people for His own possession, treasured, purchased, and set apart for God's glory. You are not odd; you are chosen and dearly loved. In a world that pressures you to blend in, this word is quiet dignity. You belong to the King. Small step: when comparison or insecurity rises, speak this truth: "I am one of His peculiar people, treasured by my Father."
entries.smallStep: Hear “treasured” when you read peculiar in Titus 2:14.

entries.title: penny
entries.summary: Small coin — worth varies by story; God counts little things.
entries.fullSummary: Penny passages matter because scripture keeps exposing heaven's different math. The coin may look small, but it becomes a lens for God's generosity, human envy, and His notice of what others ignore.
entries.smallStep: Two sparrows for a farthing logic—pennies prove divine attention.

entries.title: perfect
entries.summary: Complete, mature, finished — not flawless in every modern sense.
entries.fullSummary: "Be ye therefore perfect, even as your Father which is in heaven is perfect" calls us to mature love and wholeness. We press toward it but rest in Christ's finished work. Small step: in an area where you feel incomplete, thank God that He is making you complete in Him.
entries.smallStep: Hebrews maturity vs milk is a growth picture.

entries.title: physician
entries.summary: Healer — Christ’s mission and human humility.
entries.fullSummary: The force of the word is not admiration of medicine alone. Christ is exposing denial. Healthy people do not seek a physician; the sick do. The gospel begins where need is admitted instead of hidden.
entries.smallStep: “Physician, heal thyself” can be proverb or sarcasm—watch tone.

entries.title: predestination
entries.summary: Foreordained purpose — unto conformity to Christ.
entries.smallStep: Goal is Christlikeness, not fatalistic gloom.

entries.title: press
entries.summary: Crowd pressing in — throng around Jesus.
entries.smallStep: Physical crowd, not only “pressure” metaphor.

entries.title: prevent
entries.summary: Often “go before,” “meet,” or “come first,” not “stop.”
entries.fullSummary: In the KJV, prevent frequently means to go before someone in kindness or preparation. It is God meeting you ahead of time with mercy. When you feel behind or caught off guard by life, remember the Lord often prevents you with blessings. He goes before His people. Small step: in prayer tonight, thank Him for ways He has already gone before you this week, even the ones you have not seen yet.
entries.smallStep: In 1 Thessalonians 4:15, think “precede,” not “block.”

entries.title: propitiation
entries.summary: Wrath absorbed; mercy-seat reality — God’s justice and love meet.
entries.fullSummary: Do not flatten this into a cold formula. The word shows that at the cross God did not ignore sin; He dealt with it fully so mercy could be righteous and real.
entries.smallStep: Think “satisfied justice,” not a cold word only.

entries.title: publican
entries.summary: Tax collector — often a humbled heart versus proud religion.
entries.fullSummary: Publican becomes an important gospel word because Jesus keeps placing mercy beside religious pride. The publican in Luke 18 brings no polished record, only an honest plea, and he goes down justified.
entries.smallStep: The publican’s prayer beats the Pharisee’s posture—mercy over performance.

entries.title: quick
entries.summary: Often “living” or “alive,” not fast.
entries.fullSummary: The Word of God is "quick, and powerful, and sharper than any twoedged sword." Here quick means living and active, full of life and energy from the Holy Spirit. Jesus is the quickening Spirit. In seasons when you feel dead inside, grief, exhaustion, or spiritual dryness, this truth is medicine: His Word and His presence make dead things live again. Small step: speak one quick verse aloud over an area that feels lifeless in your life right now and thank Him that He is still the God who quickens.
entries.smallStep: Pair “quick” with “dead” in context to see alive vs lifeless.

entries.title: quicken
entries.summary: Make alive, give life, or revive — not just speed up.
entries.fullSummary: "Quicken thou me according to thy word." The same Spirit that raised Christ quickens us when we feel spiritually dead. In grief, exhaustion, or dryness, this is resurrection hope. Small step: speak this prayer over any area that feels lifeless: "Lord, quicken me according to Thy word."
entries.smallStep: Ask the Lord to quicken what feels spiritually lifeless.

entries.title: quit
entries.summary: Conduct yourself, acquit yourself — “quit like men” is courage and integrity.
entries.fullSummary: This is one of those KJV words that flips a whole verse if heard wrongly. Paul is not telling believers to give up. He is calling them to courageous, disciplined, mature bearing under pressure.
entries.smallStep: In 1 Corinthians 16:13, read quit as “carry yourself like men of faith,” not “stop.”

entries.title: raiment
entries.summary: Clothing or garments — often with symbolic meaning.
entries.smallStep: Let raiment remind you that God clothes His people well.

entries.title: redemption
entries.summary: Bought back — a price paid, ownership changed.
entries.fullSummary: Redemption answers the question of ownership. Christ does not merely improve you; He purchases you out of bondage and claims you for Himself.
entries.smallStep: Tie redemption to ransom language without sensationalism.

entries.title: reins
entries.summary: Kidneys — Hebrew idiom for inner affections; KJV uses “reins.”
entries.fullSummary: The Lord tries the reins and the heart. He knows the deepest parts of us better than we do. In battles with hidden motives or secret fears, this brings comfort and holy fear. Small step: invite the Lord to search your reins today and align them with His will.
entries.smallStep: Read as “deepest motives,” not biology quiz.

entries.title: repent
entries.summary: Change of mind that shows in turning — not mere regret.
entries.fullSummary: Repentance is not self-loathing for its own sake. It is Godward turning that agrees with the truth and walks toward mercy.
entries.smallStep: Look for fruit that matches the turning.

entries.title: replenish
entries.summary: Fill or populate the earth, not “refill an empty tank” only.
entries.smallStep: In Genesis 1:28, God fills the earth with people and life.

entries.title: reprobate
entries.summary: Disapproved, rejected after testing — serious moral and covenant language.
entries.fullSummary: This word must be handled with trembling. Paul uses it first as a call to self-examination, not as a weapon for labeling others. It presses the question of whether a life really bears the marks of truth.
entries.smallStep: In 2 Corinthians 13:5, “reprobates” is examine yourselves—not name-calling neighbors.

entries.title: reprove
entries.summary: Convict, correct, or rebuke with the goal of restoration.
entries.fullSummary: All Scripture is profitable for reproof. The Holy Spirit still gently reproves us because He loves us. In hard conversations or self-examination, receive reproof as kindness from the Lord. Small step: when conviction comes today, do not rush past it, let it lead you back to Christ.
entries.smallStep: Receive reproof as kindness when it brings you back to truth.

entries.title: resurrection
entries.summary: Standing again — Christ first, then His own.
entries.fullSummary: Resurrection is not a metaphor for vague inspiration. It is the bodily victory of Christ and the pledged future of His people.
entries.smallStep: Hope is embodied — empty tomb matters.

entries.title: revellings
entries.summary: Party excess, carousing — loud indulgence.
entries.fullSummary: Revellings are not simple gladness. They are joy detached from sobriety and truth. Scripture names them because the flesh likes celebration that asks nothing of conscience and costs dearly the next morning.
entries.smallStep: Peter reminds former patterns—freedom in Christ is clean joy.

entries.title: riot
entries.summary: Wild excess, wasteful uproar — not a modern “riot” only in streets.
entries.fullSummary: This word exposes a form of freedom that is really self-destruction. Riot is life without guardrails, where appetite burns through money, sobriety, and tomorrow. Scripture contrasts it with sober joy and Spirit-filled living.
entries.smallStep: Contrast riot with sober joy—celebration without drowning the soul.

entries.title: sanctified
entries.summary: Set apart for God; status and growth both appear.
entries.fullSummary: The KJV lets both senses stand together. Believers are sanctified in Christ, and believers are still being sanctified in the shape of daily obedience.
entries.smallStep: Note past tense “were sanctified” and ongoing “be holy.”

entries.title: science
entries.summary: Knowledge — “science falsely so called” is empty knowledge.
entries.smallStep: Not modern lab science by default — compare “knowledge.”

entries.title: shamefacedness
entries.summary: Modesty and reverence — especially in 1 Timothy 2.
entries.smallStep: Outward demeanor that matches godliness.

entries.title: simplicity
entries.summary: Sincerity, single-mindedness — not “simple-minded.”
entries.smallStep: Opposite of double-dealing.

entries.title: sod
entries.summary: Boiled or cooked — Jacob’s pottage.
entries.smallStep: “Sod pottage” is stew, not turf.

entries.title: sodden
entries.summary: Boiled — food laws and ordinary kitchen English.
entries.smallStep: Passover lamb was not sodden—God appointed roast; details teach obedience.

entries.title: soul
entries.summary: Life, self, appetite, or person — overlaps with heart and spirit.
entries.fullSummary: The word is bigger than a neat body-soul chart. Often it names the whole living person in relation to God, hunger, danger, hope, or rest.
entries.smallStep: Ask whether the verse means life, inner life, or appetite.

entries.title: spirit
entries.summary: Breath, attitude, unclean spirit, or Holy Spirit — let the verse choose.
entries.fullSummary: This is a careful-reading word. Ask whether the verse is speaking about God's Spirit, a human spirit, a spiritual atmosphere, or a creaturely spirit.
entries.smallStep: Capitalization in print helps; in audio, context must.

entries.title: stedfast
entries.summary: Steady, fixed, settled — older spelling of steadfast.
entries.fullSummary: Stedfast is quiet endurance, not stiff pride. It is the kind of constancy that keeps praying, obeying, and standing when a season tries to shake you loose.
entries.smallStep: Read stedfast as anchored faithfulness, not rigid pride.

entries.title: straightway
entries.summary: Immediately — same idea as “forthwith” in places.
entries.fullSummary: When Jesus called, the disciples followed straightway. This word pictures instant, willing obedience. In 2026 delay and distraction, the Lord still invites straightway responses. Small step: when the Spirit prompts you today, answer straightway with a quiet "yes, Lord."
entries.smallStep: Narrative speed: obey without dragging feet.

entries.title: strait
entries.summary: Narrow, tight, strict — gate, way, discipline.
entries.fullSummary: Strait does not mean cruel. Jesus is teaching that life is not found in roomy self-rule but in the narrow way that passes through repentance, faith, and obedience. The squeeze is real, but it leads somewhere living.
entries.smallStep: Strait gate is not meanness—life is found in the narrow way of Christ.

entries.title: strange
entries.summary: Foreign, alien, or unusual — context decides.
entries.smallStep: “Strange trial” is unfamiliar testing, not oddness.

entries.title: study
entries.summary: Be diligent, strive rightly — not only “academic homework.”
entries.fullSummary: "Study to shew thyself approved unto God" is a call to earnest effort and diligence in handling the Word rightly. In a distracted 2026 world, this word invites focused, quiet work before the Lord. Small step: give one undistracted portion of your day to Scripture, not to check a box, but to meet God.
entries.smallStep: 2 Timothy 2:15 is a workman approved, not proud.

entries.title: subtil
entries.summary: Crafty or shrewd — serpent in Eden, not a compliment.
entries.smallStep: Moral shade: discern good subtlety vs deception.

entries.title: suffer
entries.summary: Sometimes “allow” or “let,” not only “endure pain.”
entries.fullSummary: Jesus said, "Suffer little children to come unto me," meaning, "Let the little children come." In many places suffer simply means permit or allow. When the Lord says suffer in the sense of endurance, He never leaves you alone in it. He suffered first. Whether you are allowing good things or bearing hard things, He is with you. Small step: if something heavy needs to be suffered today, allowed or endured, bring it to Him and ask for grace to walk through it.
entries.smallStep: When children are named, “suffer” usually means “let them come.”

entries.title: sundry
entries.summary: Various, several — “sundry times” is many eras and ways.
entries.fullSummary: Sundry is not filler language in Hebrews. It highlights the patient, many-sided way God spoke before the Son came. The contrast makes Christ feel even weightier: scattered speech has now given way to final speech in Him.
entries.smallStep: Hebrews 1:1 sets up the Son—God spoke piecemeal, then perfectly in Christ.

entries.title: superstitious
entries.summary: In Acts 17, “very religious” — devout, not “irrational” only.
entries.smallStep: Paul bridges from their altar to the unknown God.

entries.title: supplication
entries.summary: Earnest asking — humble pleading prayer before God.
entries.fullSummary: This word keeps prayer low to the ground. Supplication is not performance for heaven. It is needy prayer, often specific and repeated, brought before a Father who invites you to ask.
entries.smallStep: Supplication is lowly, specific prayer — not polished speech.

entries.title: tabernacle
entries.summary: Tent of meeting; God dwelling with a moving people; shadow of Christ.
entries.fullSummary: This word is a thread of presence. From the wilderness tent to Christ dwelling among us to the final dwelling of God with man, it teaches nearness without loss of holiness.
entries.smallStep: John 1:14: “dwelt” is tabernacled among us.

entries.title: talent
entries.summary: Large unit of money in parables — capacity entrusted, not only “skill.”
entries.fullSummary: Modern talk can reduce this to personal gifting, but Jesus' parable keeps the weight on stewardship. What has been entrusted must not be buried in fear. The issue is faithful handling under the Master's return.
entries.smallStep: Parable talents test faithfulness—small or great, invest what God gave.

entries.title: tarry
entries.summary: Wait, remain, or stay a while — not just be late.
entries.fullSummary: "Tarry ye in the city of Jerusalem, until ye be endued with power from on high." Waiting on God is never wasted time. In a hurry-up world, tarry teaches us to stay until the Lord moves. Small step: when you want to rush ahead, choose to tarry in prayer and trust His timing.
entries.smallStep: Tarry in prayer instead of running ahead of God.

entries.title: temperance
entries.summary: Self-control — desires governed under grace.
entries.fullSummary: Temperance is the Spirit's gift of mastery over our appetites and reactions. In parenting, eating, screen time, or anger, temperance brings peace. Small step: in one area where you feel out of control today, ask the Holy Spirit for His temperance.
entries.smallStep: Temperance is not cold repression; it is Spirit-shaped restraint.

entries.title: temple
entries.summary: Building, Christ’s body, or believer — track the referent.
entries.smallStep: Paul’s “your body is the temple” is personal holiness.

entries.title: temptation
entries.summary: Trial or enticement — James distinguishes sources.
entries.fullSummary: Do not assume every temptation is the same thing. Some are pressures that reveal faith; others are inward pulls toward evil. Scripture gives escape, sympathy, and warning.
entries.smallStep: God does not tempt to evil; He provides escape.

entries.title: turtle
entries.summary: Turtledove — bird of the poets, not a reptile.
entries.smallStep: Song of Solomon 2:12 signals spring and return—creation praising with the singer.

entries.title: vain
entries.summary: Empty, worthless, or idols — “in vain” is emptiness.
entries.fullSummary: "Except the Lord build the house, they labour in vain." This warns against effort without God. In parenting, work, or spiritual striving, anything done apart from Him can feel empty. Small step: before a task today, quietly commit it to the Lord so it is not in vain.
entries.smallStep: “Vanity” in Ecclesiastes is vapor-like emptiness.

entries.title: variance
entries.summary: Strife, division — household and church fractures.
entries.fullSummary: Not all conflict is the same. Some variance comes from the gospel dividing false peace, and some comes from fleshly rivalry. The word is useful because it forces the reader to ask what kind of division is present.
entries.smallStep: Jesus names gospel cost—truth can split what false peace held together.

entries.title: verily
entries.summary: Truly, amen — solemn emphasis.
entries.smallStep: When Jesus doubles “Verily, verily,” slow down and listen.

entries.title: vexed
entries.summary: Troubled, tormented, or worn down — inwardly or outwardly pressed.
entries.fullSummary: Vexed is strong language for real trouble. Scripture uses it when souls are pressed, not mildly annoyed. That honesty matters because Christ meets people in true torment, not in cleaned-up summaries.
entries.smallStep: Let vexed name real torment without letting torment define the whole story.

entries.title: virtue
entries.summary: Strength, power, or moral excellence going out from Christ — not only modesty.
entries.fullSummary: When the woman with the issue of blood touched Jesus, virtue went out of Him. This was healing power, the strength and goodness of Christ flowing to those who reach for Him in faith. In your weakness, His virtue is still available. It is not something you manufacture; it is received from Him. Small step: in a moment of need today, reach for Jesus the same way, "Lord, let Your virtue touch this place in me."
entries.smallStep: In Luke 8:46, virtue is power that went out of Him.

entries.title: watch
entries.summary: Stay awake, keep guard, stay spiritually alert — especially in prayer.
entries.fullSummary: Watch is not a command to become paranoid. It is a call to stay awake to temptation, to time, and to the Lord's presence. The Bible pairs watchfulness with prayer because sleepy hearts drift fast.
entries.smallStep: Watch is active readiness, not nervous panic.

entries.title: wine
entries.summary: Fermented drink in many uses; wisdom warns excess.
entries.smallStep: Let context show celebration, medicine, or warning.

entries.title: winepress
entries.summary: Judgment image — treading out God’s wrath in Scripture imagery.
entries.smallStep: Read as sobering picture, not glee.

entries.title: wist
entries.summary: Knew — past of “wit” (to know).
entries.smallStep: Swap in “knew” when it sounds wooden.

entries.title: works
entries.summary: Deeds — not ground of salvation, yet faith without deeds is dead.
entries.fullSummary: Works do not earn union with Christ, yet true faith is never barren. Scripture refuses both prideful earning and empty profession.
entries.smallStep: Ephesians 2:8–10 holds both grace and workmanship together.

entries.title: world
entries.summary: Age, order, or people on earth — context narrows meaning.
entries.smallStep: Ask: moral system, planet, or people?

entries.title: wot
entries.summary: Know — “we wot that” means “we know that.”
entries.smallStep: Same root family as “wist.”
